checks_performed: Read only the specified source-input JSON and draft JSON; used no web sources.
Independently checked the planar-dual, colouring, Euler, face-perimeter, parity, component-count, and dual Hamiltonicity arguments.
Checked the CAI reductions, including all cases of the degree-2-path suppression construction.
Checked the quadrilateral symmetric-difference construction and its exact cycle count.

Created and ran an exact-integer checker enumerating all 512 labelled bipartite graphs on 3+3 vertices and all relevant face profiles through order 30. It found exactly nine copies of K3,3 minus one edge and one K3,3 with feedback-vertex number at least two, and all profile assertions passed.

claims.claim: The planar dual T of G is a simple Eulerian plane triangulation with a proper vertex 3-colouring I1,I2,I3, unique up to permuting the colours.
claims.evidence: A 3-connected plane graph has a polyhedral embedding and, since vertex-connectivity 3 implies edge-connectivity at least 3, its dual has neither loops nor parallel edges. Cubicity makes every dual face triangular. Every primal face is an even cycle because G is bipartite, so every dual vertex has even degree. Colouring one triangular face with three colours and propagating across adjacent triangles is consistent around every vertex precisely because its degree is even; facial boundaries generate the plane cycle space, giving global consistency. Propagation also proves uniqueness once one triangle is coloured.
claims.search_method: Direct planar-duality and colouring proof, including loop, parallel-edge, and propagation-consistency checks.

claims.claim: For each colour i, the boundaries of the primal faces corresponding to Ii are pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles covering V(G). Moreover, each colour class has total face perimeter n=|V(G)|, G has n/2+2 faces, and it has at least six quadrilateral faces.
claims.evidence: The three faces incident with each primal vertex form a dual triangle and therefore have distinct colours. Thus every primal vertex lies on exactly one face of each colour, proving disjointness, coverage, and total perimeter n. Cubicity gives |E|=3n/2 and Euler gives |F|=n/2+2. Finally, sum_f(6-|f|)=6|F|-2|E|=12. All face lengths are even and at least four, so quadrilaterals contribute 2 and all longer faces contribute at most zero; hence there are at least six quadrilaterals.
claims.search_method: Direct incidence counting and exact Euler arithmetic.

claims.claim: G is Hamiltonian if and only if V(T) can be partitioned into two sets inducing forests.
claims.evidence: Let N=|V(T)|. A two-forest partition makes every dual triangle bichromatic, hence gives exactly 2N-4 cross edges and N-2 internal edges. If the two induced forests have c1,c2 components, their internal-edge count is N-c1-c2, so c1=c2=1: both are trees. The primal edges dual to cross edges form a spanning 2-factor. If it has k cycles, its complement on the sphere has k+1 regions, exactly the components of the internal dual graph; the two trees therefore force k=1. Conversely, a Hamiltonian cycle separates the primal faces into two disks. Face adjacency within each disk is connected, and the N-2 noncycle dual edges force both induced connected graphs to be trees.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional planar-duality proof with exact edge and component counts.

claims.claim: If any bichromatic graph H=T[Ii union Ij] has a CAI-partition, then G is Hamiltonian.
claims.evidence: Write the CAI-partition as A union J, where T[A] is a tree and J is independent. If J together with the omitted colour Ik contained a cycle, connectedness of A and planarity would place A on one side. At a cycle vertex, two consecutive neighbours on the other side form a triangular face entirely in J union Ik, forcing an edge inside J, a contradiction. Thus T[J union Ik] is a forest. Claim 2 then yields a Hamiltonian cycle in G.
claims.search_method: Direct audit of the planar CAI-to-two-forests reduction.

claims.claim: In particular, G is Hamiltonian whenever some bichromatic graph T[Ii union Ij] is series-parallel.
claims.evidence: Every bichromatic graph is simple and 2-vertex-connected. The supplied source proves that every simple 2-vertex-connected series-parallel graph has a CAI-partition using a short nested open-ear decomposition: one vertex of the initial cycle enters the independent set, and each later ear is attached while preserving independence and an induced tree complement. Claim 3 then applies.
claims.search_method: Matched all hypotheses against the supplied source's Theorem 10 and audited its ear-decomposition construction.

claims.claim: For distinct colours i,j, let Qij have the i-coloured faces as vertices, with one edge for every j-coloured quadrilateral joining the two i-coloured faces opposite it. Then G has a spanning 2-factor with exactly c(Qij) cycles. In particular, connected Qij certifies Hamiltonicity.
claims.evidence: Begin with the facial 2-factor supplied by colour i. On every j-coloured quadrilateral, its two factor edges are opposite, and its two incident i-faces are distinct. Choose a spanning forest S of Qij and switch the four boundary edges of each corresponding quadrilateral. Faces of colour j are vertex-disjoint, so switches do not interfere. Inductively, every forest edge joins two distinct current cycles and its switch merges exactly those cycles. Starting with |V(Qij)| cycles and making |V(Qij)|-c(Qij) merges leaves exactly c(Qij) cycles.
claims.search_method: Exact symmetric-difference induction over a spanning forest, including loop and interference checks.

claims.claim: Every target graph on n vertices has a spanning 2-factor with at most floor((n+4)/6)-1 cycles.
claims.evidence: The two bipartition classes have equal size; simplicity and planarity exclude sizes below four, so n>=8. Let a be the smallest face-colour-class size. Then a<=floor((n/2+2)/3)=floor((n+4)/6). If a=1, its face boundary is Hamiltonian and satisfies the bound. Otherwise one of the other two colours contains a quadrilateral: if neither did, each would have at most n/6 faces, and minimality would give the same bound for a, contradicting the total n/2+2 faces. That quadrilateral supplies a nonloop edge of Qij, so c(Qij)<=a-1. Claim 5 gives the asserted 2-factor.
claims.search_method: Direct extremal face-count argument with integer floors and boundary cases.

claims.claim: Let H be 2-vertex-connected. Suppress its maximal degree-2 paths to a multigraph K, let B be the vertices of degree at least three, and let U=H[B], the unsubdivided skeleton edges. If U is a forest, or U-v is a forest for some v in B, then H has a CAI-partition.
claims.evidence: If H is a cycle, put one vertex in the independent set. Otherwise, when U is a forest, extend U to a spanning tree R of K. When U-v is a forest, put v in the independent set; 2-connectivity makes K-v connected, so extend U-v to a spanning tree R of K-v. Every remaining skeleton edge not incident with v is subdivided, because all unsubdivided edges were included in R. Select one internal vertex from each such non-tree path. These selections are mutually nonadjacent and avoid v. Their complement is the subdivided tree R with only pendant path fragments added, including fragments from paths formerly incident with v, so it is connected and acyclic.
claims.search_method: Constructive proof with separate cycle, forest, and one-vertex-deletion cases.

claims.claim: In any counterexample, every face-colour class contains at least three nonquadrilateral faces; for every colour pair, their nonquadrilateral-face adjacency graph has feedback-vertex number at least two. Moreover, every Qij is disconnected and every bichromatic graph is non-series-parallel.
claims.evidence: In a bichromatic graph, the degree of a face-vertex is half its primal face length; hence its degree-at-least-three vertices are exactly the nonquadrilateral faces, and their induced graph is U from Claim 7. A counterexample admits no bichromatic CAI-partition, so neither U nor any U-v is a forest, giving feedback-vertex number at least two. A simple bipartite graph with at most one vertex on one side is acyclic, and with two vertices on that side becomes acyclic after deleting either one; therefore every colour class has at least three nonquadrilateral faces. Connected Qij and series-parallel bichromatic graphs are excluded respectively by Claims 5 and 4.
claims.search_method: Contrapositive application of Claims 4, 5, and 7 with bipartite cycle analysis.

claims.claim: If two face-colour classes each consist of exactly three hexagons together with any number of quadrilaterals, then G is Hamiltonian.
claims.evidence: For their bichromatic graph H, U has three degree-3 vertices in each part. Exact enumeration of all 512 labelled 3-by-3 bipartite graphs found that feedback-vertex number at least two occurs only for K3,3 and the nine graphs K3,3-e. The former cannot be a planar subgraph. In the latter, the four non-endpoint vertices are degree-saturated, while each missing-edge endpoint has one remaining incidence; 2-connectivity forces the degree-2 vertices of H to form a path between those endpoints. Thus H contains a subdivision of K3,3, again contradicting planarity. Hence U has feedback-vertex number at most one, and Claims 7 and 3 give Hamiltonicity.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact enumeration of all 2^9 adjacency matrices, followed by a planar-subdivision argument.

claims.claim: Every graph satisfying the target assumptions with at most 30 vertices is Hamiltonian; consequently these arguments force every counterexample to have at least 32 vertices.
claims.evidence: Put n=2m. For colour i, let qi count quadrilaterals, ri count longer faces, and si=sum_f(|f|/2-3) over those longer faces. Exact identities give 2qi+3ri+si=m and, globally, r+s=m-4. Claim 8 gives ri>=3. Exhaustive integer enumeration found no admissible counterexample profile for m<=12 or m=14, one for m=13, and nine for m=15. Every m=13 or m=15 profile has at least two classes with ri=3 and si=0, meaning exactly three hexagons and otherwise quadrilaterals; Claim 9 applies. Cubicity forces n even, so after excluding every n<=30 the next possible order is 32.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive nonnegative-integer face-profile enumeration with exact parity and Euler constraints.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a proof that every graph satisfying the four assumptions is Hamiltonian or one explicit qualifying non-Hamiltonian graph. The draft explicitly says that it offers no full resolution or counterexample, and it does not establish either alternative. It does, however, establish material and correctly matched partial progress: dual and CAI reductions, structural necessities for any counterexample, a quantitative 2-factor bound, and Hamiltonicity through order 30. Therefore the target verdict is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, and the draft's claimed resolution of PARTIAL is ACCURATE.
